newsitem.title: UK: Timing of Russia mark Eurobond uncertain - Deutsche.
newsitem.headline: Timing of Russia mark Eurobond uncertain - Deutsche.

text.p: Russia may not launch its forthcoming jumbo mark Eurobond next week as expected if sentiment in the emerging market sector does not improve, a Deutsche Morgan Grenfell official said on Friday.

"We will launch (the Russia Eurobond) as soon as market conditions allow us to," a syndicate manager at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, joint lead manager of the deal, told Reuters in a telephone interview.

"It may be next week, but it could be the following week or whenever the market is supportive. Emerging markets are a bit weak, and we think it is better to wait until the market is not in a free fall. The issuer also thinks the same way," she said.
CSFB is joint lead manager of the transaction.

On Thursday, a Russian finance ministry official said the deal, which will be for up to 2.0 billion marks, would probably be launched on March 13 following investor presentations in Zurich and Frankfurt.
The bond, Russia's second venture into the international capital markets after a debut $1.0 billion five-year issue last November, is expected to have a seven-year maturity.
Spread talk on the deal is between 325 and 340 basis points over Bunds, but the Deutsche official said this could change to reflect moves in the spread of Russia's dollar deal.
"We will price in the area of wherever the dollar Russia bond trades at the time," the official said.
"The 325 to 340 b.p. range was set prior to the weakness of the market. If the dollar deal trades wider, we should move above the mid-300s b.p. over for the mark bond," she said.
The Deutsche official said Russia wanted to achieve a successful issue.
"We have to watch carefully what the market does. The market has become more shaky and volatile and to come up with a successful issue you really have to price it in line with the market," she said.

Russia's dollar Eurobond was trading at between 325 and 335 b.p. over U.S. Treasury notes at 12.30 GMT on Friday. The spread has been volatile since emerging market prices began a sharp decline in February amid concerns over a U.S. interest rates rise.
Russia's bond hit 350 b.p. over this week, but since its launch at 345 b.p. over has risen as high as 400 b.p.
Dealers said the spread might widen again if U.S. employment data, due for release at 1330 GMT, had a negative impact on U.S. Treasuries.
